headline: Cloud and AI revenue accelerate while profits get squeezed

kpis.label: AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue

summary_short: Revenue rose 9% year-over-year to $39.6B as AI Cloud and Compute Services grew 45%, but income from operations fell 57% to $2.2B on a goodwill impairment, an EU fine provision, and heavier AI infrastructure spending.
summary_long: Alibaba's June-quarter revenue rose 9% y/y to $39.6B, led by 45% growth in AI Cloud and Compute Services — the twelfth consecutive quarter of triple-digit AI-product revenue growth — and 45% growth in China Quick Commerce. China customer management revenue fell 7% y/y (flat like-for-like, excluding a merchant-subsidy program now booked as contra-revenue). Income from operations dropped 57% to $2.2B on a RMB4,458M goodwill impairment, a EUR550M EU Digital Services Act fine provision, and heavier technology investment; adjusted EBITA fell 30% to $4.0B. Capex jumped 75% y/y to $10.0B, driving free cash flow to a $6.6B outflow. Cash and liquid investments fell to $69.9B, from RMB520.8B at March 31. No new guidance was issued in the release.
confidence_notes: Segment reporting was restructured this quarter (Alibaba E-commerce Group / AI Cloud and Compute Services / AI Labs and Applications / All Others replace the prior structure); segment y/y comparisons use the release's own recast prior-period figures, which may not exactly match previously published segment cuts. The resolver's pre-populated eps_usd shard value (8.52, unit 'USD') appears to be a currency-label mismatch — the filing states RMB8.52 as the Non-GAAP diluted EPS per ADS, with US$1.26 as the actual USD-equivalent figure; this summary uses the filing's own USD figure instead. The March 31, 2026 cash balance is presented in RMB only because the release gives no USD translation for that date (a different FX rate applied) and this summary does not compute one.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by 45% growth in AI Cloud and Compute Services and 45% growth in China Quick Commerce (Freshippo, Taobao Instant Commerce), partly offset by a 7% y/y decline in customer management revenue.
Decrease driven by lower adjusted EBITA, a RMB4,458 million goodwill impairment in All Others, and a provision for a EUR550 million EU Digital Services Act fine.
Decline reflects heavier technology investment, only partly offset by better Cloud segment results and efficiency gains elsewhere in the business.
Margin compression follows directly from adjusted EBITA falling 30% while revenue rose 9% — a smaller profit pool spread over a larger revenue base.
Decline reflects the same drivers as adjusted EBITA — heavier technology investment, partly offset by improved Cloud performance and efficiency gains elsewhere.
EPS decline closely tracks the 38% fall in non-GAAP net income, with the modestly larger per-ADS decline reflecting a slight increase in diluted share count.

drivers.metric: AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue
drivers.explanation: Acceleration driven by broader public-cloud adoption and rising demand for AI-related products, which delivered a twelfth consecutive quarter of triple-digit growth.
Outflow widened mainly due to a 75% year-over-year increase in cloud infrastructure capital expenditure.
Decrease from March 31 driven by the free-cash-flow outflow and unfavorable FX translation, partly offset by net proceeds from new bank borrowings.
Increase reflects procurement-cycle timing, added compute capacity for anticipated AI-agent adoption, and higher pricing across a broad range of chip components.

Management frames the quarter as strong top-line and Cloud momentum funded by heavier AI investment, which is compressing near-term profits; the CEO cites accelerating full-stack AI commercialization as the core strategic driver.
